transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-30
Start time (UTC): 14:00
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jordan (MarlinWorks Head of ML), Priya (MarlinWorks Platform Eng), Sam (MarlinWorks CTO)

Summary: quick discovery focused on per-token pricing, batching/caching levers, and hosting tradeoffs (hosted vs private). Customer has strict data residency and KMS requirements for some datasets but would like to keep high-volume non-sensitive traffic hosted if unit cost allows.

Topics: per-token math, average vs peak qps, batching window impacts on 95th pct latency, KV/prefix cache usage, dedicated pools and reserved capacity, SOC2/KMS + private control plane details.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. With me is Ethan, our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Ethan: Hey, hi all. Quick agenda — understand your traffic patterns, cost constraints, latency SLOs, and which data must stay private. We'll then walk through levers (batching, cache, quantization) and hosting options.
[00:21] Jordan: Thanks. I'm Jordan, Head of ML at MarlinWorks. We're evaluating whether we can route most workloads to hosted to save ops, but we have a subset of sensitive customer data that must stay in our cloud region and behind our KMS.
[00:33] Priya: And I'm Priya on platform, I'll need to know networking requirements for Private deployment and what's required for SSO and logs.
[00:39] Sam: Sam here, CTO — main ask is: can you show the unit economics so we can compare hosted per-token with our own internal costs including Ops?

[00:50] Ethan: Totally. Can you give approximate traffic? tokens per request, and qps?
[00:55] Jordan: Right now we're at 7 req/s for the high-volume endpoint, average payload ~400 tokens in, 150 tokens out on completion prompts, so ~550 tokens per transaction. Peak bursts hit 40 req/s during certain windows.
[01:15] Ethan: OK, that helps. For a hosted scenario our published per-token rate for standard seq models is X (--- note: some values transcribed roughly ---), but the key is effective cost after batching and cache. If you allow a 50ms batching window we can coalesce requests and reduce per-token cost 20-30% depending on model.
[01:36] Jordan: 50ms window — that sounds like it could hurt P95 latency. Our SLO is 200ms P95 for the interactive path.
[01:43] Ethan: Right, there's a trade. For 200ms P95 you can still use small batching (20-30ms) and get a good compromise. Also prefix/K-V cache is huge for repeated prompts — if you have repeated system prompts or warm prefixes, hit rate matters. We see cases where cache reduces tokens emitted by 10-40% depending on prompt reuse.
[02:05] Priya: How does cache work across hosted vs private? If the cache is customer-specific and sensitive, does it need to be in their VPC?
[02:12] Ethan: Good question. In hosted we can do customer-isolated cache that respects data residency, but for maximum control you can run Redwood Private with a customer-managed control plane where KV stays in your VPC and keys in your KMS. Hosted can still be configured to not store prompt content long-term and to route sensitive requests to a private pool.
[02:30] Sam: Curious about Dedicated — reserved GPU pools. If we did Dedicated for the sensitive subset, can we still spill to hosted for non-sensitive traffic?
[02:38] Maya: Yes, that's one of the common patterns — hybrid routing. You can pin sensitive routes to Dedicated or Private and route everything else to Hosted. That gives cost savings while meeting residency and KMS needs.
[02:48] Jordan: Ok, show the math. If we have 550 tokens per tx at 7 rps baseline and 40 rps peak, what's our monthly token volume and cost?
[02:58] Ethan: Quick calc — at 7 rps sustained that's about 7 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 30 ≈ 18M requests/month, times 550 tokens ~= 9.9B tokens monthly baseline. Peak periods raise that but depends on burst shape. Per-token hosted rate (for example) is transcribed here roughly at $0.000012 / token for generation and $0.000003 / token for prompts — again POI, we'll send exact published numbers in the spreadsheet. With caching and batching that effective cost drops.
[03:29] Priya: Those per-token numbers seem higher than our internal GPU TCO. If we self-host, factoring infra + ops + engineers, we think about $0.000008 per token — is that realistic?
[03:41] Ethan: Possible, but important to include ops cost (oncall, upgrades, quantization effort), and peak provisioning inefficiency. Also model variants: if you quantize and run int8, you reduce GPU cost but may need quality validation. Redwood Optimize helps suggest quant profiles per workload.
[04:01] Jordan: What's the typical commit for Dedicated? We might not want a year-long reserved contract.
[04:08] Maya: We have monthly reserved options with predictable throughput SLAs; annual gives you better pricing. We can prototype with a small Dedicated pool for the sensitive routes and keep the rest hosted.
[04:18] Sam: On security — SAML/SSO and audit logs are must-haves. Also we need end-to-end encryption with our KMS when private.
[04:26] Ethan: We support SAML, RBAC, and audit logs. For Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. For Hosted you can bring-your-own-key for some flows and we redact or avoid storing payloads; for full control Private is preferred.
[04:40] Priya: Network egress costs are also a factor for us with cross-region traffic. If we use Private in our region, how does Redwood handle data plane placement?
[04:49] Ethan: Private can be deployed inside your VPC or on-prem with data plane colocated to minimize egress. Hosted runs in multiple regions and you can route to the nearest. We'll include bandwidth/cost sketches in the follow-up.
[04:59] Jordan: Back to batching — you mentioned a 20-30ms window for low latency. How much unit cost reduction do we realistically see?
[05:06] Ethan: Example: without batching you pay full per-token for every request. With continuous batching sized to your peak concurrency we often see 10-25% per-token improvement at 20ms windows, and 25-45% at 50-100ms windows. These are sensitive to request size distribution. If you have many requests with long sequences, batching helps less.
[05:25] Jordan: And quantization — is that per-model or per-tenant? What's the risk to quality?
[05:31] Ethan: Per-model variant; we can host multiple variants and route by policy. Quantization (int8/4-bit) reduces memory and increases throughput but can cause subtle quality regressions. Redwood Optimize runs evals on your prompt set to score regressions and recommends safe profiles.
[05:46] Priya: Do you support mixing models? For example, a smaller model for cheap completions and a larger one for critical outputs?
[05:53] Maya: Yes — smart routing can route by intent, by confidence, or by cost tier. You can start on Hosted with routing rules and then move the sensitive ones to Private/Dedicated.
[06:01] Sam: What's the expected time to pilot? We want to spin up by mid-August if possible.
[06:06] Maya: We can get a pilot running in 2-3 weeks for hosted. Private pilot depends on infra approvals but typical timelines are 3-6 weeks.
[06:14] Jordan: For the pilot, can you simulate our traffic or run a dry-run so we can validate cost?
[06:19] Ethan: Yes — we can ingest your sample traces and run a synthetic replay against our hosted and dedicated configs to produce a cost model and latency matrix. We'll need a representative 1-2 day trace and the prompt templates.
[06:30] Priya: On logging/data retention — we need 90-day audit logs for the sensitive product. What's retention policy?
[06:36] Maya: Hosted default retention is 30 days, enterprise add-on increases retention. Private you control retention. We'll include retention options and pricing.
[06:44] Jordan: Any limitations on models in Private versus Hosted? We have some custom fine-tuned models.
[06:49] Ethan: Private supports self-hosted fine-tunes; we can onboard custom models but need the model artifacts and compatibility checks. For hosted we also support customer models via secure uploads under some agreements.
[06:59] [00:07:00] Jordan: Let's talk about an example cost scenario — assume we route 60% non-sensitive to hosted, 40% sensitive to Dedicated. How does that change numbers?
[07:09] Ethan: If baseline tokens 9.9B/month, splitting reduces hosted bill to ~6B tokens and Dedicated covers 4B. Dedicated has a fixed reserved cost plus a lower per-token marginal. The math often shows hosted for high variance volume and Dedicated for steady base load gives best unit economics. We'll send a modeled spreadsheet.
[07:28] Sam: Are there any hidden fees — egress or storage or model licensing?
[07:33] Maya: Bandwidth is billed separately in some configs, model licensing usually included for open models but proprietary model licenses are extra. We'll list everything in the quote.
[07:42] Priya: For our compliance team: do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO?
[07:46] Maya: Yes, we'll attach our SOC2 and ISO docs. For Private we also provide deployment checklists for auditors.
[07:54] Jordan: On expected accuracy changes with quantization, do you have a framework to measure that?
[07:59] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Optimize runs A/B and evaluation suites against your prompt set and gives delta metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-like or embedding drift, plus qualitative checks). We can show a sample report.
[08:10] [00:08:10] Priya: Network— if we want the Private control plane in our account, do you require special permissions?
[08:16] Ethan: We'll provide a Terraform module and minimal IAM role for deployment. For air-gapped on-prem, there's an installer and support for HSM/KMS.
[08:25] Jordan: Ok, let's get concrete: what do you need from us to run the cost model?
[08:29] Ethan: A 48-hour trace of requests (timestamps, token counts), sample prompt templates, and a list of which routes are sensitive. Also desired latency SLOs.
[08:37] Jordan: We can get that by 2026-08-03.
[08:41] Maya: Great. We'll follow up with the spreadsheet and a proposed pilot scope.
[08:46] Sam: One last question — competitors: we looked at Anthropic for better safety tooling and Vertex for ease of plug-in. How does Redwood compare on unit cost?
[08:55] Maya: We focus on production unit economics and routing flexibility, and our Optimize tooling to reduce cost via batching/caching. We'll include a competitive positioning sheet.
[09:04] [00:09:04] Jordan: Thanks — recap and next steps?
[09:08] Maya: Recap: Jordan to deliver traces + prompt templates by 2026-08-03. Maya to send costing spreadsheet and SOC2/KMS notes by 2026-07-31. Ethan to produce quick latency baseline and initial cost model for hybrid split by 2026-08-04. Schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2026-08-10.
[09:26] Priya: Sounds good.
[09:28] Sam: Thank you.
[09:30] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links to docs and the spreadsheet.

End of transcript.

Notes about transcription: occasional word errors (e.g., K-V cache transcribed as K V cache), numbers approximate, model per-token rates left generic in-conversation — exact published rates will be in follow-up spreadsheet.
